newsitem.title: FRANCE: March data to show French jobless rise over - Juppe.
newsitem.headline: March data to show French jobless rise over - Juppe.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday that March jobless data would show that the rise in unemployment was coming to an end.
"Since 1993 it (unemployment) has totally stabilised and the latest figures for March will show that the rise has in fact been brought to a halt," Juppe said.

"This is not a result which lives up to either my hopes or my objectives. I'm stating that clearly. But things have begun to change," he said during a presentation of the centre-right coalition's joint manifesto for the parliamentary election.
Unemployment hit a record 12.8 percent in February and the March figures are due out on Wednesday, in the middle of the campaign before the two-round election on May 25 and June 1.

But the figures are seen as highly volatile and the jobless rate, which is calculated differently and based on International Labour Organisation criteria which exclude people who did some part-time work in the month, rose to 12.8 from 12.7 percent.
Economists have been predicting that the unemployment rate will remain at 12.8 percent in the March data.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis also sounded an optimistic note on unemployment in a face-to-face debate with Socialist former finance minister Michel Sapin on LCI television.

Arthuis said that, with a cautious official forecast of 2.3 percent growth in 1997, the economy would create 120,000-140,000 jobs this year but that it would take a few more months for a turnaround from a trend of increasing unemployment.
"My conviction is that with (1997) growth of 2.3 percent -- a cautious forecast -- we will create 120,000 to 140,000 jobs," he said.

"I know that for a few more months there will still be a considerable number of people entering the labour market for the first time. We know that in the coming months there will not be a downward turn in unemployment. But we are in a turnaround phase, we're on the eve of job creation which is estimated at 250,000 for 1998, he said.
The European Commission said last week it was forecasting French unemployment of 12.5 percent for 1997 and 12.1 percent unemployment in 1998.
The International Monetary Fund also issued forecasts last week, predicting French unemployment at 12.8 percent this year and 12.3 percent next year.
